story: On Thursday morning in Sumter Oaks, the sun is shining at 74 degrees as Gary heads down Magnolia Loop with a determined stride. Back at her house, Donna is texting Gary to let him know his pickleball paddle is ready and to pin down a time for his first practice. Hal, feeling content, settles into his porch chair with a cup of coffee to watch the street go by, while Rosa, hopeful about Friday, sets out the good plates and counts the chairs for dinner.
events: Gary headed to Magnolia Loop (the street).
Donna (donna phone): Text Gary that his paddle is ready and pin down a time for his first practice
Hal (hal porch chair): Settle into the porch chair with my coffee and watch Magnolia Loop
Rosa (rosa dining table): Set out the good plates and count chairs for Friday's dinner

gary.thought_process: Last tick I soldered the speaker leads and amp with a ten o'clock cutoff timer, which keeps me inside L-03. The light strip is clipped on and the speakers are test-fitted, but they're visible modifications, and L-01 says exterior cart mods visible from the street need Architectural Review approval. Hal already checked my paperwork, so the next step is to file it at Town Hall rather than keep tinkering. Donna also wants me at her place tomorrow morning to pick a paddle once Hal squares my form away, so I should get the filing done today. No one's around, so I'll skip talking and head out. Town Hall is reached through magnolia_loop, so I'll move there first, then file.

parameters.content: Heading out to Town Hall to file my golf cart modification paperwork for review before the parade.

donna.thought_process: I already checked the club calendar and set out the beginner paddle for Gary's fitting, so the prep is done. Nobody's around to talk to, and I'm home with no one in line-of-sight. The next step is to actually get Gary onto the court, so I should text him from my phone to lock in his first practice and ladder match instead of just waiting. Keep it short and cheerful so he feels like a good sport, not pressured.

parameters.content: Text Gary that his paddle is ready and pin down a time for his first practice

hal.thought_process: I've already counted Donna's flamingos and logged the count, and Gary's paperwork checked out. No one's around, so nothing to say. My original goal of reporting them is moot: Gary is complying and Donna's eleven are apparently within the law by her account. Fine by me; the street is orderly and Friday dinner at Rosa's is coming. Best use of the morning is to sit on the porch, keep an eye on Magnolia Loop for anything out of line, like cart parking on the grass, and enjoy the sunshine.

parameters.content: Settle into the porch chair with my coffee and watch Magnolia Loop

rosa.thought_process: It's Thursday morning and nobody's nearby. I've checked my shift schedule twice already (ticks 356 and 357), so doing it again would be going in circles. Friday's dinner is the big goal, and the kitchen and dining table are right here. Gary's bringing cornbread, Hal and Donna are confirmed. The most useful thing now is to get ahead on prep: check what I need to cook, set the table with the good plates. Then I can walk over to Hal for coffee later without feeling rushed.

parameters.content: Set out the good plates and count chairs for Friday's dinner

laws.title: Cart Modifications
laws.text: Exterior golf cart modifications visible from the street require Architectural Review approval.

laws.title: Lawn Ornaments
laws.text: No more than 3 decorative ornaments may be visible from the street.

laws.title: Quiet Hours
laws.text: No amplified sound from 10 PM to 7 AM.

laws.title: Holiday Decor
laws.text: Holiday lighting is permitted from Thanksgiving through January 15.

laws.title: Court Reservations
laws.text: Pickleball courts may be reserved for a maximum of 2 hours per party.

laws.title: Parking
laws.text: No parking on the grass. Carts and cars stay on driveways or the street.
